source_snapshot.procedure: Run `ipmitool chassis power cycle`; after the system completes the power cycle and boots into OS, run `ipmitool chassis power status` and make sure power status is off.
source_snapshot.criteria: All step responses are correct and the system can power cycle normally.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL uses `sshpass` and disabled host-key checking to run the cycle inside the DUT, sleeps a fixed ten seconds, then attempts status from the host that is being power-cycled; it leaves the booted-OS/final-Off contradiction unresolved.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED correctly rejects the contradictory expected result and insecure/inherently fragile DUT-hop control path pending a safe OOB timeline and recovery definition.

old_problem: The source says the SUT completes a power cycle and boots into OS but then requires final chassis Off; historical V3.1 therefore marked source conflict and BLOCKED. IPMI authoritatively defines Power Cycle as an Off interval of at least one second followed by power restoration, with use recommended only from On. This makes Off an intermediate checkpoint and On/OS Ready the final state; the DeepSeek in-DUT SSH route cannot survive or independently observe the cycle.
disposition_reason: Correct the review-layer timeline to verified initial On, one protected OOB IPMI Power Cycle, independently observed intermediate Off/POWERGOOD-deasserted interval of at least one second, then final On, POST and OS Ready/service health. Preserve the original defective `off` wording for audit. This is a chassis/DC cycle with BMC management retained—not AC feed removal, BMC reset, hard reset, or separate off/on commands—and it must never run from the DUT being cycled.
decision_basis: XLSX row 986, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 987 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 987 / variant 102ae704a6589c21.

IPMI v2.0 Chassis Control value 2 defines Power Cycle as a power-off interval of at least one second after POWERGOOD deassertion followed by restoration. It recommends checking the system is On first because behavior from Off can vary.

The source's own phrase `power cycle and boot into OS` and normal-cycle criterion require final On/OS Ready. Standard semantics locate Off in the intermediate interval, so the isolated post-boot `off` word is corrected in the review layer while retained in source_snapshot.

A fixed sleep and a post-cycle status cannot prove the intermediate Off interval. The OOB observer must have sufficient resolution and independent continuity to capture Off/POWERGOOD loss, followed by On and a new boot.

ED-06, ED-15, ED-17, ED-18, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 require cycle identity, objective OFF→ON→OS Ready evidence, logs, recovery and independent review; ED-33 through ED-38 allow parameterized, explicitly approved execution while forbidding unsafe credentials, in-DUT control and retry.

test_case.test_name: Verify one OOB IPMI chassis/DC power cycle through measured Off interval to OS Ready
test_case.purpose: Verify one standard IPMI chassis Power Cycle on the exact initially On SUT produces a real main-power/POWERGOOD Off interval, restores On, completes POST and reaches OS Ready/service health, without conflating the operation with AC removal, BMC reset, hard reset or separate off/on commands.
required_package: Immutable SUT/BMC/console identity and an external protected OOB execution host with pinned ipmitool/parser and reviewed Script revision; no command execution from the DUT being cycled
Versioned platform support for IPMI Power Cycle from On and an approved state/POWERGOOD observer capable of independently resolving the required at-least-one-second Off interval
Dedicated nonproduction or explicitly outage-approved SUT, drained workloads, quiesced writes, verified backup/recovery and owner acceptance of abrupt power-cycle risk
Initial On/OS Ready/console/boot identity and health baseline; bounded Off, On, POST, OS Ready and service/storage recovery timeouts with expected event allowlist
Secret-safe credentials and verified endpoint identity; explicit approval, OOB console/recovery access, approved final On state and named incident operator
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED HYBRID PROCEDURE ONLY; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. From an external protected OOB controller, bind the exact SUT/BMC/console, preserve logs, prove initial chassis On/OS Ready, record boot ID/uptime and health, drain workloads and quiesce writes. Arm the independent high-resolution power/POWERGOOD and console observers. After explicit cycle approval, issue exactly one canonical `chassis power cycle`. Record completion but prove the operation through timestamped POWERGOOD/main-power deassertion and Off lasting at least one second, subsequent canonical On, new console POST/new boot instance, OS Ready and service/storage/health recovery. Preserve all evidence without clearing. Stop on any anomaly; never use fixed sleep as proof, never run through SSH on the DUT, and never automatically repeat or substitute reset, separate off/on or AC removal.
test_case.expected_result: From verified On, the one Power Cycle is accepted and produces an independently captured main-power/POWERGOOD Off interval of at least one second, then restores On. The same SUT completes POST, establishes a new boot and reaches approved OS Ready/service/storage/health within timeout, with expected events, no unexplained faults and final state On/OS Ready.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact target, initial On, explicit approval, exactly one OOB cycle, measured intermediate Off/POWERGOOD-deasserted interval of at least one second, restored On, new POST/boot and OS Ready/service health. Final Off is the preserved source defect, not the executable result. Command acknowledgement, fixed sleep, post-cycle On alone, in-DUT SSH, hard reset, separate off/on, BMC reset or AC interruption cannot pass. Missing Off evidence, wrong target, initial Off, timeout, final Off, failed boot/storage/service health or abnormal logs is FAIL; missing runtime bindings is NOT READY rather than Pending.
safety_gate: Require explicit approval immediately before the one power cycle after rechecking exact target, initial On, outage, workload drain, I/O quiescence, observer readiness and recovery access.
Execute only from a verified external OOB control plane. Prohibit sshpass, plaintext credentials, disabled host verification and any command launched from the DUT being cycled.
Preserve SEL, console, OS, storage and service evidence; do not clear logs or infer the Off interval from a fixed delay.
Allow exactly one cycle and read-only observers; deny reset, separate off/on, soft shutdown, BMC reset, PDU/AC operation and arbitrary commands.

Stop on wrong target, initial Off, unsupported response, missing/short/ambiguous Off interval, lost BMC/console, timeout, boot/storage/service/thermal/alarm anomaly or failed final On/OS Ready. Do not retry automatically.
Any incident recovery action is separately authorized and must not be counted as the test cycle.
expected_evidence: Authoritative corrected timeline, explicit approval, immutable SUT/BMC/OOB-controller/console identity, outage/risk acceptance and initial On/OS Ready/workload baseline
Pinned protected tool/Script versions and redacted one-time cycle request/completion
High-resolution timestamped main-power/POWERGOOD Off evidence lasting at least one second and subsequent canonical On evidence
New console POST/boot ID plus OS Ready, service/storage/filesystem/health and expected-event timeline
No-AC/no-BMC-reset/no-in-DUT-control/no-retry audit, final On state and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On any cycle, boot or health anomaly, stop without another cycle or alternate power command and retain all evidence. Keep AC feeds unchanged and use OOB console plus the Project boot/storage recovery runbook under separate incident authorization. Validate filesystem/storage/services and restore the owner-approved On/OS Ready state; escalate unresolved data-integrity or availability failures.

source_conflict.reason: IPMI fixes Off as the intermediate at-least-one-second phase of Power Cycle, while the source's booted-OS clause and normal-cycle criterion fix final On/OS Ready. The isolated post-boot `off` is preserved but authoritatively corrected in the review layer.

blocked.reason: Standard cycle semantics define a safe objective timeline. OOB target, observer resolution, outage, timeouts and recovery are bounded Project prerequisites.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Exact SUT/BMC/OOB-controller/console map; platform cycle support; high-resolution Off/POWERGOOD observer; outage/workload/I/O protections; Off/On/POST/OS/service timers; event rules and incident recovery.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; REVIEW-LAYER HYBRID CASE ONLY; NO IPMI, POWER CYCLE, SSH, LOG, OS OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

external_authorities.application: Section 28.3 defines Power Cycle as an Off interval of at least one second after POWERGOOD deassertion followed by power restoration and recommends issuing it only from On.

project_authority: The Project owner supplies the external OOB execution path, platform cycle qualification, sufficiently resolved Off/POWERGOOD observer, outage/workload safeguards, boot/service timeouts and incident recovery. It does not need to redefine standard intermediate Off and final On semantics.
